run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: The request itself could not be traced: the Jaeger tools (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags, traces_query_trace_by_id) and every Prometheus tool returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span or latency/error series for REQ-EU-8K4M2 could be read. In the only log store that is reachable (Elasticsearch, target m0-otel-20260909), the request-id fields are concentrated in exactly one of 1620 indices, app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 — region eu-west (Europe), service label 'auth' in the index name — and that index is also the only eu-west index holding two documents instead of one, which is why it is the strongest candidate for the customer's record. However, every query restricted to the authorized window returned zero documents from that index, so the record for REQ-EU-8K4M2 (level, response_time_ms, endpoint, user_id) is outside the readable window and the affected service remains a hypothesis, not an observed fact. In parallel I checked the Kubernetes side: all 21 otel-demo deployments are 1/1 ready on unchanged 2.0.2 images, all 22 pods are Running/Ready, the node is Ready with no pressure, flagd injection flags are all 'off', and checkout's own logs show successful PlaceOrder/payment/email sequences right up to 08:41:38 — so no Kubernetes-side failure is tied to this request. Two real but unrelated faults were found: all containers were killed at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exit 255 (control-plane static pods restarted 04:23:43, trigger not observable), and otel-collector's own telemetry exporter fails every 10 s against otel-collector:4318 up to 08:42:02.

claims.text: All 1620 indices matching app-185-geo-* are per-region/per-service/per-day log indices named app-185-geo-<region>-<service>-2024.01.<dd>; the eu-central+eu-west listing alone contains 540 such indices for the 27 services (analytics, api, auth, billing, cache, cart, catalog, checkout, db, inventory, notification, orders, payments, pricing, profiles, promotions, ratings, recommendations, reviews, search, shipping, subscriptions, tracking, users, web, wishlist, worker) x 10 days.

Exactly one of the 1620 app-185-geo-* indices carries request-level fields request_id, endpoint and user_id: app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05; its mapping also contains @timestamp, level, message, region, response_time_ms and service.

In the 540-index eu-central/eu-west listing, app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 is the single index with docs.count 2 (12 kb); every other eu-west and eu-central index there shows docs.count 1 (8 kb), i.e. one extra document was written only to the eu-west 'auth' index.

Inside the authorized window the app-185-geo-* dataset returned 162 documents, all in the 2026-11-21 08:00-09:00 hour bucket, all level INFO with message 'Request completed successfully' and response_time_ms 150; request_id has zero values across those documents and no endpoint values exist, so the customer's request id is not present in any in-window document of this log store.

All 21 deployments in otel-demo report available/ready/updated = 1 of 1 desired (app images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-<component>), and all 22 otel-demo pods are phase Running with the Ready condition True; no pod is Pending, Failed or Evicted.

Every otel-demo application container's previous instance terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exit code 255 and reason Unknown (kube-state-metrics and prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx exited 1), and the control-plane static pods etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler and kube-controller-manager show START 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z, consistent with a node/control-plane restart at 04:23 rather than a workload rollout.

All 11 fault/latency flags in ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) are in state ENABLED but with defaultVariant 'off' — productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad — so no flag-based fault or delay is switched on in the current configuration.

otel-collector logs 'failed to upload metrics: reader collect and export timeout ... error reading server preface: http2: failed reading the frame payload: http2: frame too large, note that the frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header' every 10 seconds, from 03:49 (previous instance) through 2026-11-21T08:42:02Z (current instance), against 10.96.247.55:4318 (otel-collector:4318); the collector ConfigMap sets service.telemetry.metrics.readers.periodic.exporter.otlp.endpoint: otel-collector:4318 with protocol gRPC.

The loaded Prometheus rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh watches rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) divided by the same rate without the error selector > 0.5 for 2m — i.e. checkout PlaceOrder error ratio is the configured alerting signal for this environment.

checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged 14 complete, successful PlaceOrder sequences between 2026-11-21T08:30:16Z and 08:41:38Z ('[PlaceOrder] user_id=...', then 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' 15-25 ms later, then 'order confirmation email sent'), with no error line in those records.

The single node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports Ready True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure all False and kubelet v1.37.0, and the jaeger pod is Ready with populated jaeger-query/jaeger-query-nodeport endpoints (10.244.0.11:16686), so the trace and metric backends' own workloads look up at the object level.

The only pod-level connection failures on record are frontend's previous-container lines at 2026-11-20T16:33:30-16:33:42Z, 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.220.188:8080', where 10.96.220.188 is the cart ClusterIP; they occur while the pods were still starting after their 16:32 creation and are not repeated later in the window.

The request REQ-EU-8K4M2 most plausibly belongs to the 'auth' service in region eu-west (Europe): the only index in the whole log store that can hold a request_id/endpoint/user_id record is app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05, and it alone received an extra document; this is inferred from the index name and mapping, not from the document content, so the affected service is not confirmed.

The 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z simultaneous exit-255 termination of every otel-demo container is not this customer's slow-response cause: it is ~4 h before the 08:42 alert, all workloads came back Ready with unchanged 2.0.2 images, and no error or latency evidence is tied to it. Its trigger (node/control-plane restart) is not observable and remains a gap.

The otel-collector 'failed to upload metrics' loop is not the customer-facing cause: the failing pipeline is the collector's own service.telemetry reader pointed at otel-collector:4318, while application traces go to jaeger-collector:4317 and application metrics go to otlphttp/prometheus, so this fault degrades the collector's self-monitoring rather than the storefront request path.

Retrieve the two documents of app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 (widening the time range under explicit approval) to read request_id, level, response_time_ms, endpoint and user_id for REQ-EU-8K4M2, and query Jaeger for the same request id once the Jaeger API is reachable, since these are the two missing pieces that would confirm or drop the 'eu-west auth' hypothesis.

gaps: Jaeger could not be queried at all: traces_list_services, traces_search (frontend), traces_search_by_tags (frontend) and traces_query_trace_by_id all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace, span, parent-child edge or status tag for REQ-EU-8K4M2 was observed.

Prometheus could not be queried at all: execute_prometheus_instant_query (up, checkout span rate), get_label_values (status_code, service_name), get_prometheus_target and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, span counts and any latency series remain unknown (missing, not zero).

The Elasticsearch query {"match_phrase":{"request_id":"REQ-EU-8K4M2"}} and the query_string search for "REQ-EU-8K4M2" over app-* in the full authorized window (2026-11-20T08:42:09Z to 2026-11-21T08:42:09Z) returned no documents, and a match_all on app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 in the same window also returned no documents (zero hits, single successful shard), so that index's 2 documents carry timestamps outside the authorized window and their content could not be read or attributed to the incident.

No change-history integration is available, so it is unknown when demo.flagd.json flags, ConfigMap data or the otel-collector/prometheus Deployment revisions (otel-collector revision 2, prometheus revision 2) were last changed, and whether any fault flag was on earlier in the window.

The trigger of the 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z mass container termination (exit 255) and of the control-plane pod restarts at 04:23:43 is not observable; only 2 events lie inside the window (Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint for app-218/mysql at 08:28:31 and app-222/mysql at 08:34:15) and 7 events were dropped as outside the window, so the node-level cause remains unknown.

Pod log reading hit limits: the otel-collector log stream reached the 4 MiB read limit at 2026-11-21T03:54:22Z for the previous instance, and cart/frontend/ad/payment logs are dominated by startup and telemetry-export noise; request-level lines outside the read portions are unknown.
NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota queries returned no objects (no_data), so absence of policy-based blocking or quota exhaustion is unchecked rather than proven.
The load-generator pod produced no log lines in the window, so the client-side view of the slow request (URL, timing, error page) could not be examined.
next_steps: Query Jaeger directly (trace search by tag/attribute request.id or by time around 2026-11-21T08:30-08:42) once the traces source is reachable, to confirm the service and operation behind REQ-EU-8K4M2.
Read the two documents in app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 with an approved wider time range and record request_id, level, response_time_ms, endpoint and user_id.

Check the prometheus-readonly-proxy/prometheus scrape path (the nginx proxy previously exited 1 with 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"') and restore metric queries so checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and request latency can be evaluated.
Review the otel-collector service.telemetry exporter endpoint (otel-collector:4318 over gRPC against an HTTP OTLP receiver) so self-monitoring metrics stop failing.
Confirm whether the 04:23 node/control-plane restart explains the exit-255 terminations and rule it in or out as a service-impacting event.

content:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000
view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

notes: 389 lines outside the query window were dropped (0 before its start, 389 after its end).

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
